purpose: What each GetYourGuide widget searches for, per article. scripts/balance-gyg-widgets.mjs reads this. Edit here, not in the script, and never in the markdown - the balancer rewrites the markdown every time it runs.
slots: Slot 1 is the subject: what the page is about. Slots 2 and 3 are big sellers: named high-value products drawn from the pool named in anchorGroup, which is where the basket value is. Slot 4, which only the longest pages reach, is the article's 'adjacent' product - the thing someone reading it would also buy, never a repeat of slot 1 - or another big seller when it names none. A page never shows the same query twice. An article may also name slot3 or slot4 explicitly to override the pool. Rob, 15 September 2026: the second widget sells the big products rather than the adjacent one.
howToPickAQuery: Name a product, not a category. 'Tower of London tickets' returns bookable inventory; 'London top attractions' returns a vague mix. If you cannot name a product a reader of this page would plausibly buy, leave 'adjacent' out rather than filling it.

howPicksWork: A slot may be "pick:<name>" instead of a search string, which pins the widget to those exact activity ids via data-gyg-tour-ids. Use a pick where the search returns the wrong thing. A probe of all 159 queries on 4 September 2026 (data/gyg-query-probe.json) found 49 where no result was on the subject, several returning other countries entirely - Auckland for a Thames cruise, Venice for the Natural History Museum, Sonoma for Kenwood House. Re-run scripts/probe-gyg-queries.mjs before trusting any query you add. 19 September 2026: every pool entry is now a pick rather than a search, because a search returns three versions of one product - three Stonehenge coach trips, three London Eye tickets - and Rob asked for each widget to offer three different things.
